title: Welder
description: Fundamentals of welding processes and safe workplace organisation. Joint preparation, equipment, protection and inspection. A training programme for work in the Republic of Kazakhstan.

slides.title: Welder
body: Fundamentals of welding processes and safe workplace organisation.
Joint preparation, equipment, protection and inspection.
A training programme for work in the Republic of Kazakhstan.
slides.callout: This course does not automatically award a vocational grade.

slides.title: Course content
body: The course covers arc welding, gas flame processes and equipment.
Separate sections address electrical, gas and fire hazards.
Practical scenarios connect preparation, execution and completion.
slides.callout: The welding procedure specifies parameters for the actual task.

slides.title: Purpose of a welded joint
body: Welding creates a permanent joint between materials.
Required properties depend on the material, structure and operating conditions.
Weld appearance does not verify all internal properties.
Acceptance follows the requirements for the specific product.
slides.callout: Structural safety depends on joint quality.

slides.title: Main processes
body: An electric arc provides heat in arc welding.
Gas welding uses the flame of fuel gas and oxygen.
Weld-pool protection depends on the selected process.
Select the process according to material, thickness and procedure.
slides.callout: One set of parameters cannot apply to every process.

slides.title: Manual metal arc welding
body: The consumable electrode contributes to the weld metal.
Its coating provides the intended process protection.
Select the electrode classification, diameter and parameters using the welding procedure.
Electrode condition affects joint quality.
slides.callout: Damp or unsuitable materials must be replaced.

slides.title: Gas-shielded welding
body: The process uses wire or a non-consumable electrode, depending on its type.
Gas shields the weld pool from the surrounding atmosphere.
Interrupted gas supply can impair quality.
Select the gas and flow rate according to the procedure and equipment.
slides.callout: Shielding gas can displace oxygen from the work area.

slides.title: Gas welding and cutting
body: The torch or cutting torch must match the gas used.
Gas welding and oxygen cutting perform different tasks.
Select parameters and equipment according to the material and manufacturer's instructions.
Use the lighting and shutdown sequence for the actual equipment.
slides.callout: There is no universal pressure setting for all torches.

slides.title: Task documentation
body: Read the drawing and joint requirements before work.
Establish the material, edge preparation and welding position.
Check the procedure, parameters and inspection requirements.
Clarify unclear requirements before welding starts.
slides.callout: An informal assumption cannot replace the specified procedure.

slides.title: Preparing components
body: Clean surfaces as required by the procedure.
Remove contamination that could impair quality or produce harmful emissions.
Check edge shape and joint gap.
Secure components for stable positioning and safe access.
slides.callout: Assess an unknown coating before heating it.

slides.title: Assembly and tack welds
body: Verify component alignment against the drawing.
Make tack welds according to material and procedure requirements.
Fixtures must hold components without dangerous movement.
Remove unacceptable tack-weld defects using the established method.
slides.callout: Tack welds also affect joint quality.

slides.title: Parameters and sequence
body: Select current, voltage and travel speed using the procedure.
Account for welding position, thickness and the component's thermal condition.
Any parameter change must be justified.
Pass sequence helps control shape and distortion.
slides.callout: Guessing parameters is especially dangerous for safety-critical structures.

slides.title: Welding power sources
body: Transformers, rectifiers and inverters have different characteristics.
Verify power supply and permitted load against the equipment passport.
Follow the cooling and duty-cycle instructions.
Stop in the event of overheating or a fault.
slides.callout: A compact machine still requires correct connection.

slides.title: Cables and electrode holder
body: Check insulation, connections and electrode clamping.
Protect cables from heat, cuts and moving vehicles.
Place the holder to prevent accidental short circuits.
Remove defective components from use.
slides.callout: Correct damaged insulation before energising.

slides.title: Work return conductor
body: Current must return through the intended welding circuit.
Provide a reliable connection to the workpiece.
Do not substitute random pipes or structures for the return conductor.
Apply the special insulation requirements in fire or explosion hazardous conditions.
slides.callout: The welding circuit and protective earthing serve different purposes.

slides.title: Permanent and temporary welding stations
body: A permanent station is equipped for repeated operations.
A temporary station requires assessment of the actual task location.
Access, lighting and equipment positioning must be safe.
Coordinate nearby activities before starting.
slides.callout: Moving the machine creates a new workplace.

slides.title: Main welding hazards
body: The arc creates radiation and electrical shock hazards.
Sparks and hot metal cause burns and fires.
Fumes and gases affect breathing.
Handling components, noise and awkward posture create additional risks.
slides.callout: Select protection for all hazards of the task.

slides.title: Eye and face protection
body: Select a welding helmet or shield for the process and parameters.
The filter must provide the required protection.
Check integrity, attachments and function.
Use protection against flying particles during grinding and cleaning.
slides.callout: Ordinary glasses cannot replace a welding filter.

slides.title: Clothing and hand protection
body: Clothing must protect against sparks and hot particles.
Use welding gloves and keep them dry.
Prevent exposed skin and pockets that collect sparks.
Footwear and clothing arrangement must keep hot metal out.
slides.callout: Clothing contaminated with combustible substances is unsuitable.

slides.title: Protecting other people
body: Separate the welding area with the specified screens.
Prevent unprotected people from looking directly at the arc.
Check where sparks and particles travel.
Keep access routes clear and easy to identify.
slides.callout: Arc hazards extend beyond the welding station.

slides.title: Fumes and ventilation
body: Remove contaminants as close to their source as possible.
General ventilation supplements local extraction.
Emissions depend on the metal, coatings and consumables.
Select respiratory protection from a risk assessment; it does not replace required ventilation.
slides.callout: The absence of a strong smell does not prove clean air.

slides.title: Electrical safety for welders
body: Authorised personnel connect the machine using the established method.
Check protective connections and cables before work.
Do not work with damaged equipment or unsafe moisture conditions.
Repairs and switching require the relevant separate authorisation.
slides.callout: An electrical safety group does not authorise every operation.

slides.title: Pre-shift checks
body: Clarify the task, documentation and authorisation.
Inspect the machine, cables, fixtures and protective equipment.
Check ventilation, screens and fire precautions.
Correct deficiencies before welding.
slides.callout: The check applies to today's location and task.

slides.title: Preparing hot work
body: Obtain the prescribed authorisation for temporary hot work.
Remove or protect combustible materials.
Check openings and adjoining spaces.
Provide firefighting equipment and the required monitoring.
slides.callout: Sparks can cause smouldering out of sight.

slides.title: Oxygen and fuel gases
body: Oxygen supports combustion and increases fire hazards.
Fuel gas can form a dangerous mixture with air.
Keep oxygen fittings free from oil and grease.
Never use oxygen to blow off clothing or ventilate a space.
slides.callout: Each gas requires compatible equipment.

slides.title: Identifying a cylinder
body: Identify the gas from markings and documentation.
Check the shell, valve and required examination information.
Do not use a defective or uncertainly identified cylinder.
Colour alone is not sufficient for connection.
slides.callout: Uncertainty about the contents rules out connection.

slides.title: Positioning and moving cylinders
body: Secure cylinders against falling and protect them from heat.
Use equipment intended for cylinder handling.
Do not lift by the valve or expose cylinders to impacts.
Determine separation distances and co-location from current requirements.
slides.callout: Valve damage can cause a sudden release.

slides.title: Regulators and gauges
body: Select a regulator for the gas and pressure range.
Use compatible connections without improvised adapters.
Check gauge condition and absence of damage.
Set operating pressure according to the torch instructions.
slides.callout: A value from someone else's example is not a setting.

slides.title: Hoses and connections
body: Use hoses suitable for the gas and working conditions.
Protect them from kinks, sparks and mechanical damage.
Use the specified fasteners for connections.
Check leaks by an approved method without an open flame.
slides.callout: A smell or suspected leak requires stopping.

slides.title: Flashback and protection
body: Flashback carries the flame back towards the gas system.
Specified valves and flashback arrestors reduce the risk.
Stop according to the instructions after a pop, overheating or unstable operation.
Restart only after establishing and correcting the cause.
slides.callout: A safety device does not replace a serviceable system.

slides.title: Welding containers
body: Before heating, establish what the container previously held.
Remove residues and isolate connected services under the procedure.
Test the atmosphere and complete the required authorisation measures.
Do not independently weld a closed or unidentified container.
slides.callout: An apparently empty container may contain flammable vapours.

slides.title: Confined spaces
body: Entry requires special preparation and established authorisation.
Arrange atmosphere testing, ventilation, communication and an attendant.
Plan rescue without improvisation.
Stop and leave if conditions change.
slides.callout: Shielding gas can create an oxygen-deficient atmosphere.

slides.title: Work at height
body: Use a safe platform and the specified fall protection.
Select attachment points under the established system, not arbitrarily.
Protect fall-protection components from sparks and hot metal.
Barrier off the lower area against falling objects and particles.
slides.callout: A random scaffold component is not a verified anchorage.

slides.title: Handling components
body: Determine mass and the handling method beforehand.
Use suitable lifting equipment and stable supports.
Keep hands clear of potential trapping points.
Identify hot components and place them safely.
slides.callout: Metal appearance does not always reveal its temperature.

slides.title: Making the weld
body: Maintain the parameters and sequence specified by the procedure.
Monitor process stability and equipment condition.
Carry out the required cleaning between passes.
Do not continue if equipment fails or protection is lost.
slides.callout: Stop for unsafe conditions before a defective joint results.

slides.title: Visible joint defects
body: Cracks, undercut, overlap and unfilled craters require assessment.
Weld size and shape must match the documentation.
Porosity and lack of penetration can have different causes.
Determine acceptance from requirements, not personal impressions.
slides.callout: Grinding does not prove removal of an internal defect.

slides.title: Inspection and repair
body: Supplement visual inspection with the required methods.
Record results against the specific joint.
Use an agreed procedure for repair.
Repeat inspection to confirm the repair result.
slides.callout: Unauthorised repair can conceal the cause of a defect.

slides.title: Breaks and completion
body: Shut down equipment and the gas system as instructed.
Prevent unintended starting and leaks.
Inspect the work area and adjacent spaces for smouldering.
Record completion and maintain the required fire monitoring.
slides.callout: Cooling and concealed smouldering require attention after welding.

slides.title: Faults or leakage
body: Stop work and carry out a safe shutdown.
Warn people and notify the responsible person.
Do not search for gas leaks with a flame or repair under pressure.
Resume only after the cause has been confirmed as corrected.
slides.callout: Repeated popping is not normal operation.

slides.title: Fire and emergency notification
body: Report the exact location and nature of the hazard.
Call for help under the established procedure; use 112 or 101 where necessary.
Maintain a safe escape route.
Attempt firefighting only with suitable training and safe conditions.
slides.callout: Evacuate when fire threatens to spread.

slides.title: First aid and safety
body: First stop harmful exposure without endangering yourself.
Call emergency services and act within your training.
For electrical injury, do not touch the person until electrical exposure is safely removed.
Do not enter a hazardous atmosphere without protection to attempt rescue.
slides.callout: Assistance requires safe conditions.

slides.title: Scenario: an unidentified container
body: You are asked to weld an attachment onto a used container.
Its previous contents are unknown.
Stop until identification, preparation and authorisation are complete.
External cleanliness does not prove absence of hazardous residues.
slides.callout: Heat only after safe conditions are verified.

slides.title: Final knowledge assessment
body: The welding procedure determines materials, preparation and parameters.
Check equipment and protective measures before work.
Faults, leaks and changed conditions require stopping.
Select Start test.
slides.callout: Safe completion is part of every welding task.
